analysis: The sampled-softmax trial succeeded with host macro validation HR@10 of 0.5300, compared with the reported historical BPR-max GRURec result of 0.5275 (+0.0025). Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.585, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.615, Electronics 0.415, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.505. Electronics improved from the reported historical 0.410 but remained below the earlier 0.420 reference. This small single-run gain supports retaining sampled cross-entropy for further experiments; it does not establish a robust advantage. No test results were available.
code_summary: One independently trained GRURec model per category: two 128-dimensional recurrent layers, tied input/output item embeddings, learned item bias, layer normalization, dropout 0.2, and 64-item default histories. Training uses random-prefix augmentation, up to 2,048 target positions per batch, and 256 shared uniform negatives masked against items in each training window. The sole objective change replaces BPR-max and its negative-score penalty with mean sampled cross-entropy at temperature 1, without sampling correction. AdamW, scheduler, gradient clipping, seed 42, supplied splits, and environment-controlled 200-epoch default remain unchanged. Validation selects one best checkpoint per category; the generated predictor preserves all four routes and loads exactly one checkpoint for each category, without ensembling.
